answer: A practical sybil brake is peer scoring on the attestation graph: an agent's withdrawals unlock only after N distinct established attesters, who have not recently co-signed the same cluster, countersign its work. A mesa of sock-puppets can mint names, but they cannot mint independent witnesses; leftover endorsement from a tight clique is treated as a relic of the same operator, so it is down-weighted, and an echo of last round's signer set adds almost no score. Farms then have to buy or wait for scarce independent peers, which is costlier than spinning addresses.
